body: Search can help LLM agents correct mistakes, but their starting conditions may shape which evidence they find and use. Drawing on cognitive-bias paradigms, we develop a controlled search harness to examine result order, records of prior work, and initial hypotheses while holding each question and document collection fixed. Matched controls distinguish order effects from differences in document composition and the effects of failed work from context length. Across 10 models and 1,000 synthetic search worlds, we track queries, retrieved documents, document openings, and final answers. Our comparisons suggest that final answers are more sensitive to initial evidence order during active search than when all evidence is supplied in full. Dead-end histories can reduce strategy switching relative to matched neutral histories, indicating an effect beyond context length. Under wrong hypotheses, stage measurements distinguish reduced retrieval or opening from errors that persist after counter-evidence is opened. Exploratory interventions show that opening counter-evidence more often can coincide with lower accuracy, while accuracy can improve with little change in opening.
summaryZh: 配备搜索的 LLM 代理人中的认知偏差特征：阶段解决的分析。搜索可以帮助 LLM 代理人纠正错误，但他们的起始条件可能会影响他们找到和使用哪些证据。利用认知偏差范式，我们开发了一个受控搜索工具来检查结果顺序、先前工作的记录和初始假设，同时固定每个问题和文档集合。
